text:
ConocoPhillips fell 3.3% today as crude oil prices tumbled—U.S. crude dropped below $100 a barrel after Trump signaled openness to talks with Iran at the UN, easing some of the immediate geopolitical premium that had been supporting prices. The stock has given back most of a two-week rally, sliding 5% overall as traders reassess the outlook for oil demand and supply disruptions in the Middle East.

The timing matters: earlier in the week, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown and escalating Houthi attacks had pushed prices higher and kept tension elevated, but today's diplomatic signal reversed that momentum. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly reduce the profit margin on every barrel sold, which is why the stock moved down sharply in line with the commodity.
